newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's institutions to offer loans at low rate.
newsitem.headline: Japan's institutions to offer loans at low rate.

text.p: Three Japanese public finance institutions plan to offer low-interest loans to companies developing new technologies, officials at the institutions said on Monday.
They said the loans would carry interest rates below the rate for a loan from the government's treasury investment and loan programme.

The Japan Development Bank, Japan Finance Corporation for Small Business and North East Finance of Japan said they plan to offer loans with interest rates 50 basis points below the loan programme's annual rate of 3.0 percent.
They expect to begin offering the loans from the start of the fiscal year in April. The loans will be offered for two years.
During fiscal 1997, Japan Development will provide up to about 50 billion yen worth of loans, Japan Finance up to about 7 billion and North East Finance up to about 3 billion.
"Presently, we are planning to offer loans at 50 basis points below the rate of government's loan programme, but we still have to see the market trends in April," said a Japan Development official.
The rate of the government's programme fluctuates in line with market's trends.
The public institutions are aiming to provide loans for the development of a wide range of technologies, including telecommunications and broadcasting, the officials said.
Priority is expected to be given to projects to development medical treatments, they said.
